newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close weaker with U.S. after auctions.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close weaker with U.S. after auctions.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in moderate trade on Wednesday, pulled lower by U.S. treasuries after bond auctions in both countries, dealers said.

"All we're seeing here is (traders) continuing to mark it down slowly but surely with the U.S. There really has not been any big bias here in Canada one way or the other," said a bond trader at one bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.45 to C$108.50 to yield 7.270 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond fell 16/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
The spread between the benchmark 30-year bonds was 44 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Tuesday.
Canadian bonds drifted lower with U.S. treasuries, which weakened amid concern about Thursday's five-year auction. The U.S. market eased this afternoon after the auction there of two-year bonds.

The Canadian market saw the auction of C$1.3 billion of 8.0 percent Government of Canada bonds due June 1, 2027. The auction produced an average yield of 7.299 percent and price of C$108.495. Bids from primary dealers totaled C$3.04 billion, including C$63.75 million of non-competitive tenders.

The injection of new 30-year supply in Canada helped to weaken the market slightly, said Ted Carmichael, head of research with J.P. Morgan Canada. Dealers said the decline in prices following the Canadian auction sparked increased interest from accounts

In economic news, Statistics Canada reported that Canadian retail sales rose 0.9 percent in November, above forecasts for a 0.6 percent rise. Bond investors are now looking ahead to the release of Canada's consumer price index (CPI) for December on Thursday. The unadjusted December CPI is forecast to rise 0.2 percent.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.39 to C$102.93 to yield 6.589 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.55 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to four basis points from one basis point at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.79 percent against the U.S. bill which last yielded 5.17 percent.
